method: Independent authored Codex reviewer walkthroughs after reading current user-story SKILL.md. Only prompt fields extracted from Product fixtures; other reviewer outputs not read. Not a runtime routing benchmark or stochastic success rate.

cases.prompt: Write a job story for a field inspector. When coverage drops while submitting a completed inspection, keep the report on device, show pending status, and retry without duplicating it when the connection returns. We have no mockups yet.
cases.output:
Title: Submit an inspection through a coverage interruption.
When coverage drops while I submit a completed inspection, I want the report kept and submitted after reconnection, so I can finish the visit without losing my work or creating duplicates.
Design: not provided.
Acceptance criteria:
1. The completed report remains on the device while offline.
2. The report shows a pending status while submission is pending.
3. When connectivity returns, submission is retried.
4. Retrying does not create a duplicate inspection report.

cases.prompt: Create a JTBD job story: at monthly payroll cutoff the finance lead needs to see unapproved timesheets so nobody is accidentally omitted. List employee, period and approval status; filter to unapproved. Do not design reminders or escalation.
cases.output:
Title: Find unapproved timesheets at payroll cutoff.
When monthly payroll cutoff arrives, I want to see which timesheets are still unapproved, so I can identify people at risk of being accidentally omitted.
Design: not provided.
Acceptance criteria:
1. Each listed timesheet identifies the employee, period, and approval status.
2. Filtering to unapproved shows only timesheets whose approval is outstanding.
Scope: reminders and escalation are excluded.

cases.prompt: Write a role-first user story with Given/When/Then for a workspace admin revoking a member's access. Active sessions must end and future sign-in must be denied.
cases.output:
Title: Revoke workspace membership access.
As a workspace admin, I want to revoke a member's access, so that they can no longer use the workspace.
Scenario: Revocation ends current and future workspace access.
Given a member has access to the workspace and active sessions
When the workspace admin revokes that member's access
Then the member's active workspace sessions end
And subsequent sign-in attempts to that workspace are denied.
Open scope question: whether revocation must also disable the person's account outside this workspace; this story assumes workspace access only.
